worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3v-7u+7 \\ v-2u+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7u+3v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot (-7)-3\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 2 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 2 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-7 \\ y-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1\cdot (x-7)+3\cdot (y-3) \\ -2\cdot (x-7)+7\cdot (y-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-x+3y-2 \\ -2x+7y-7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=(-1)x+3y-2,\,v=-2x+7y+(-7).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-1+3+(-7)=-5.
$$
